did_you_know.text: Did you know? David gathered thirty thousand of Israel’s finest men to bring up the Ark of God, turning its transport into a large-scale national undertaking.
Did you know? In this chapter, the Ark is called both the “Ark of God” and the ark over which the name of the LORD of Hosts, who is enthroned above the cherubim, is proclaimed.
Did you know? On the first attempt, the Ark was carried on a new cart from the house of Abinadab, and Uzzah and his brother Ahio guided the cart.
Did you know? The procession was accompanied by joy and music: the people played wooden instruments, lyres, harps, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.
Did you know? When the oxen shook the Ark, Uzzah reached out and grasped it. As a result, the LORD struck him, and he died there.
Did you know? After Uzzah’s death, David was afraid of the LORD and asked, “How can the Ark of the LORD come to me?” Therefore, he did not immediately bring the Ark to the City of David.
Did you know? The Ark remained in the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite for three months, during which time the LORD blessed Obed-Edom and his entire household.
Did you know? When the Ark was brought up from the house of Obed-Edom, David sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf after the bearers of the Ark had taken six steps.
Did you know? David danced before the LORD with all his strength, wearing a linen ephod, expressing his great joy at the Ark’s arrival in the City of David.

Did you know? After placing the Ark in the tent, David blessed the people and gave every man and woman a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins. Then all the people returned to their homes.
